headline: University student beaten to death in Khulna over meal dispute
summary: A 22-year-old North Western University student died after being assaulted by fellow mess members over allegations of eating food without permission and theft.
details: Md. Ajmal Hossain, a first-year English student at North Western University, died after being assaulted by other members of the private mess where he lived in the Islam Nagar area of Khulna.
The incident occurred on Friday night when Ajmal allegedly ate a meal without notifying the mess authorities, violating the house rules that required notification two hours in advance.

Following a heated argument, other mess members reportedly took Ajmal to the roof of the five-story building, where they beat him and cut his hair. During the assault, he reportedly fell from the roof.
The victim's father stated that Ajmal called him around 9 PM on Friday, claiming he was being accused of theft. He further alleged that some mess members demanded 1 lakh BDT from him over the phone.
The mess cook stated that Ajmal had admitted to eating the food without permission, but other members accused him of stealing rice, money, mobile phones, and laptops.

Police from the Harin Tana police station have confirmed that their investigation found evidence of the beating. They have seized a stick used in the assault and are analyzing phone records (CDR) to investigate the extortion attempt.
North Western University authorities have described the death as mysterious and called for swift administrative action.
caption:
A university student was beaten to death in Khulna after allegedly eating a meal without permission in his mess.

Md. Ajmal Hossain, a first-year English student at North Western University, died after being assaulted by other members of the private mess where he lived in the Islam Nagar area of Khulna.

The incident occurred on Friday night when Ajmal allegedly ate a meal without notifying the mess authorities, violating the house rules that required notification two hours in advance.

Following a heated argument, other mess members reportedly took Ajmal to the roof of the five-story building, where they beat him and cut his hair. During the assault, he reportedly fell from the roof.

The victim's father stated that Ajmal called him around 9 PM on Friday, claiming he was being accused of theft. He further alleged that some mess members demanded 1 lakh BDT from him over the phone.

The mess cook stated that Ajmal had admitted to eating the food without permission, but other members accused him of stealing rice, money, mobile phones, and laptops.

Police from the Harin Tana police station have confirmed that their investigation found evidence of the beating. They have seized a stick used in the assault and are analyzing phone records (CDR) to investigate the extortion attempt.

North Western University authorities have described the death as mysterious and called for swift administrative action.

headline_marked: Up to 100% increase: [[Govt pensions redefined redefined under new pay scale]]
headline: Up to 100% increase: Govt pensions redefined redefined under new pay scale
summary: The government has issued a notification for the new pay scale, redefining net pensions for retirees and lifelong family pensioners with increases up to 100%.
details: The government has redefined the net pensions for retirees and lifelong family pensioners under the new pay scale, with increases ranging from 55% to 100%.
For those with a net pension of 9,000 BDT or less as of June 30, 2026, the increase will be 100%, making the minimum net pension 10,000 BDT and the maximum 18,000 BDT.
Pensioners receiving between 9,001 BDT and 20,000 BDT will see a 75% increase, with a new range of 18,001 BDT to 35,000 BDT.
Those receiving 20,001 BDT to 30,000 BDT will receive a 65% increase, the minimum being 35,001 BDT and the maximum 49,000 BDT.
For pensioners with 30,001 BDT to 40,000 BDT, the increase will be 60%, with the new range being 49,001 BDT to 62,000 BDT.
Pensioners receiving 40,001 BDT or more will see a 55% increase, with a minimum of 62,001 BDT and the maximum capped at 70,200 BDT.
Retirees already receiving more than 70,200 BDT will continue to receive their existing net pension until the next annual increase on July 1, 2027.
Existing special benefits for net pension recipients will be abolished from the date the new pay scale takes effect.
From July 1, 2026, if a serving employee dies, their family will receive pension, gratuity, and other allowances according to the prevailing family pension rules.
caption:
Government pensions are getting a major boost! Retirees can see increases of up to 100% under the new pay scale.

The government has redefined the net pensions for retirees and lifelong family pensioners under the new pay scale, with increases ranging from 55% to 100%.

For those with a net pension of 9,000 BDT or less as of June 30, 2026, the increase will be 100%, making the minimum net pension 10,000 BDT and the maximum 18,000 BDT.

Pensioners receiving between 9,001 BDT and 20,000 BDT will see a 75% increase, with a new range of 18,001 BDT to 35,000 BDT.

Those receiving 20,001 BDT to 30,000 BDT will receive a 65% increase, the minimum being 35,001 BDT and the maximum 49,000 BDT.

For pensioners with 30,001 BDT to 40,000 BDT, the increase will be 60%, with the new range being 49,001 BDT to 62,000 BDT.

Pensioners receiving 40,001 BDT or more will see a 55% increase, with a minimum of 62,001 BDT and the maximum capped at 70,200 BDT.

Retirees already receiving more than 70,200 BDT will continue to receive their existing net pension until the next annual increase on July 1, 2027.

Existing special benefits for net pension recipients will be abolished from the date the new pay scale takes effect.

From July 1, 2026, if a serving employee dies, their family will receive pension, gratuity, and other allowances according to the prevailing family pension rules.
